KUJF32/35 refers to a specific set of SKS (Sundhedsvæsenets Klassifikationssystem) procedure codes used in the Danish healthcare system to define a colonoscopy performed with or without a biopsy [^src1]. These codes are a critical component of the Danish Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) quality database, DANIBD, specifically serving as the technical mechanism to track postoperative follow-up care [^src1].

In the context of national quality development for IBD care, KUJF32/35 is directly tied to [[indikator-3|Indicator 3]], which measures the rate of postoperative colonoscopies following ileocecal resection in patients with Crohn's disease [^src1]. For a patient to be considered as having received the recommended postoperative follow-up under this indicator, the colonoscopy must be performed within one year of the surgery date, and the procedure must be registered using the KUJF32/35 codes [^src1]. 

The implementation of these codes for tracking purposes was formalized when Indicator 3 was introduced into the system on October 1, 2022 [^src1]. Alongside other related surgical and procedural codes, KUJF32/35 enables standardized measurement across regions and departments, helping to identify both excellent clinical practices and areas requiring improvement in postoperative IBD care [^src1].
